the question whether and how employees' smartphone use after and/or during work affects their work engagement and psychological detachment.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

intensive smartphone use after the workday is detrimental to psychological detachment, whereas the same is true for work engagement only when intensive smartphone use occurs during the workday and when employees experience high telepressure.

intensive smartphone use during the workday can undermine work engagement only if workplace telepressure is present, but intensive smartphone use after the workday can hamper psychological detachment irrespective of whether workplace telepressure is experienced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the smartphone is a tool that allows employees to be productive and efficient, but it also has the potential to undermine their work-life balance and work engagement.
smartphone use after work can have detrimental effects on employees' recovery, and smartphone use during work can have detrimental consequences on their engagement.
intensive smartphone use during the day and in the evening is associated with negative outcomes, and this association is stronger when employees experience high telepressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employees' smartphone use during work is associated with their work engagement, but only to the extent that workplace telepressure is high.
